Formulation
Predisposing: History of unspecified mental health issues; chronic asthma.  
Precipitating: Recent onset of systemic physical illness (fatigue, aches) of unclear etiology.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing physical symptoms impairing concentration, exercise, appetite.  
Protective: Supportive marital relationship, employment, currently positive mood, engaged with medical care.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Maintain current positive mood while physical investigations proceed.  
  • Prevent recurrence of past mental health issues.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Monitor mood during work-up of physical illness.  
  • Provide early intervention if depressive/anxiety symptoms emerge.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Report any drop in mood, increased anxiety, or thoughts of self-harm promptly.  
  • Continue normal routine, graded exercise as tolerated.  
  • Utilise existing supports (wife, colleagues).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Screen mood and anxiety at follow-up appointment (post blood tests).  
  • Provide psychoeducation on interaction between chronic physical symptoms and mood.  
  • Consider formal mental health screening tools (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) if symptoms develop.

Secondary Problem (history of unspecified mental health difficulties):
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Identify early warning signs from past episodes.  
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Clarify past psychiatric history for accurate risk profile.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Prepare timeline of any previous mental health treatment to discuss at review.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Explore past diagnoses, treatments, family psychiatric history at next consult.  
  • Decide on need for referral to psychology/psychiatry if indicated.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Importance of blood tests, potential tick-borne infection, physical-mental health link (documented plan to monitor mood).
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Emergence of persistent low mood, anhedonia, significant anxiety, sleep disturbance, hopelessness.
- Coping Strategies: Maintain activity within energy limits; pacing, balanced diet, restful sleep hygiene; communicate early with GP.

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Obtained verbally.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable.
- Review Date: To coincide with follow-up blood-test review (approx. 1 week post-testing) or sooner if mood deteriorates.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Comprehensive mental health history, full MSE, formal cognitive assessment, emergency contact details, smoking status clarification, family psychiatric history, explicit consent documentation.  
● Internal conflicts from the transcript: None detected.  
● Transcript quality notes: Single telehealth consultation focused predominantly on physical concerns; minimal mental health data available; some audio dropouts leading to incomplete smoking history.
